paragraphs.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔וא וַיֵּ֥רֶד יְהוּדָ֖ה מֵאֵ֣ת אֶחָ֑יו וַיֵּ֛ט עַד־אִ֥ישׁ עֲדֻלָּמִ֖י וּשְׁמ֥וֹ חִירָֽה׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass at that time, that Yehudah went down from his brethren, and turned in to a certain Adullamite, whose name was Hirah.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּרְא־שָׁ֧ם יְהוּדָ֛ה בַּת־אִ֥ישׁ כְּנַעֲנִ֖י וּשְׁמ֣וֹ שׁ֑וּעַ וַיִּקָּחֶ֖הָ וַיָּבֹ֥א אֵלֶֽיהָ׃

i18n.en: And Yehudah saw there a daughter of a certain Kena'anite whose name was Shua; and he took her, and went in unto her.

paragraphs.text: וַתַּ֖הַר וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ עֵֽר׃

i18n.en: And she conceived, and bore a son; and he called his name Er.

paragraphs.text: וַתַּ֥הַר ע֖וֹד וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ אוֹנָֽן׃

i18n.en: And she conceived again, and bore a son; and she called his name Onan.

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּ֤סֶף עוֹד֙ וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֔ן וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ שֵׁלָ֑ה וְהָיָ֥ה בִכְזִ֖יב בְּלִדְתָּ֥הּ אֹתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And she yet again bore a son, and called his name Shelah; and he was at Khziv when she bore him.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקַּ֧ח יְהוּדָ֛ה אִשָּׁ֖ה לְעֵ֣ר בְּכוֹר֑וֹ וּשְׁמָ֖הּ תָּמָֽר׃

i18n.en: And Yehudah took a wife for Er his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֗י עֵ֚ר בְּכ֣וֹר יְהוּדָ֔ה רַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיְמִתֵ֖הוּ יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: And Er, Yehudah's firstborn, was wicked in the eyes of YHWH; and YHWH slew him.

paragraphs.commentary: The Tetragrammaton (יְהוָה) is rendered **YHWH**, the established corpus convention. The Translator flagged a discrepancy between the task brief (which called for "Yahweh") and the stable Genesis text, which renders the Tetragrammaton uniformly as "YHWH" (verified at chs 15:1, 18:1, 22:11, 28:13, and across all twenty prior occurrences). The convention is confirmed and applied here and at v 10; "Yahweh" is deferred to any future corpus-wide retransliteration pass. No glossary entry; this is a corpus-convention confirmation, not a lexical decision.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוּדָה֙ לְאוֹנָ֔ן בֹּ֛א אֶל־אֵ֥שֶׁת אָחִ֖יךָ וְיַבֵּ֣ם אֹתָ֑הּ וְהָקֵ֥ם זֶ֖רַע לְאָחִֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: And Yehudah said unto Onan, Go in unto thy brother's wife, and perform the duty of a husband's brother unto her, and raise up seed to thy brother.

paragraphs.commentary:
*ve-yabbem otah* is the technical verb of **levirate marriage** — the Piel of y-b-m, denominative from *yavam* ("husband's brother") and *yevamah* (the widow on whom the duty falls). When a man dies sonless, his brother takes the widow and the firstborn of that union is reckoned to the dead man, so his name and line survive. The ASV-baseline periphrasis "perform the duty of a husband's brother" is retained because it correctly conveys a *duty* attaching to the brother-in-law, not an ordinary marriage. The institution is codified in Deut 25:5-10 (with the *chalitzah* sandal-ceremony for the brother who refuses) and is the legal substrate of Ruth 4 (the redemption-marriage producing David's grandfather); the cross-corpus reach is why the lemma is centrally housed (`yibbum-levirate-marriage-institution`).

*ve-haqem zera le-achikha* ("raise up **seed** to thy brother") carries the chapter's legal engine: the offspring is reckoned to the dead brother, not the levir. The ASV-baseline "seed" is kept so the single lexeme *zera* repeats audibly across vv 8-9 (command → refusal). The existing central *zera* entries (the covenant-promise, the dust/stars/sand triad) do **not** govern this levirate-progeny sense; the chapter-specific deployment is housed in the overlay (`zera-levirate-progeny-raise-up-seed`). See HALOT s.v. *ybm*; Sarna *JPS Genesis* pp. 266-267; Westbrook *Property and the Family in Biblical Law* 1991.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֣דַע אוֹנָ֔ן כִּ֛י לֹּ֥א ל֖וֹ יִהְיֶ֣ה הַזָּ֑רַע וְהָיָ֞ה אִם־בָּ֨א אֶל־אֵ֤שֶׁת אָחִיו֙ וְשִׁחֵ֣ת אַ֔רְצָה לְבִלְתִּ֥י נְתָן־זֶ֖רַע לְאָחִֽיו׃

i18n.en: And Onan knew that the seed would not be his; and it came to pass, when he went in unto his brother's wife, that he spilled it on the ground, lest he should give seed to his brother.

paragraphs.commentary: *ve-shichet artzah* ("and he **spilled it on the ground**") is a euphemism. The verb is the Piel of *shachat* — core sense "to spoil, ruin, mar, destroy" (the same verb used of the corruption that brought the Flood, Gen 6:11-12) — not literally "to spill"; the object is left unexpressed in the Hebrew, part of the verse's euphemistic reticence. The ASV-baseline "spilled it on the ground" is the established decorous rendering and is kept. The strong verb sets Onan's *shichet* ("ruin", v 9) pointedly against Yehudah's *haqem* ("raise up", v 8): he ruins the seed rather than raising it, and the act is judged *ra* ("evil", v 10). The thrice-repeated *zera* ("seed") binds the refusal to the command; "seed" is retained for that reason (`zera-levirate-progeny-raise-up-seed`). See HALOT s.v. *shachat*; Sarna *JPS Genesis* p. 267.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֛רַע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה וַיָּ֖מֶת גַּם־אֹתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And the thing which he did was evil in the eyes of YHWH; and he slew him also.

paragraphs.commentary: *va-yera be-eynei YHWH* ("was **evil** in the eyes of YHWH") echoes the verdict on Er (*ra be-eynei YHWH*, v 7) with the same root, framing both deaths as divine judgement on the brothers' conduct. The Tetragrammaton is rendered **YHWH** per the corpus convention confirmed at v 7.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוּדָה֩ לְתָמָ֨ר כַּלָּת֜וֹ שְׁבִ֧י אַלְמָנָ֣ה בֵית־אָבִ֗יךְ עַד־יִגְדַּל֙ שֵׁלָ֣ה בְנִ֔י כִּ֣י אָמַ֔ר פֶּן־יָמ֥וּת גַּם־ה֖וּא כְּאֶחָ֑יו וַתֵּ֣לֶךְ תָּמָ֔ר וַתֵּ֖שֶׁב בֵּ֥ית אָבִֽיהָ׃

i18n.en: Then said Yehudah to Tamar his daughter-in-law, Remain a widow in thy father's house, till Shelah my son be grown up; for he said, Lest he also die, like his brethren. And Tamar went and dwelt in her father's house.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּרְבּוּ֙ הַיָּמִ֔ים וַתָּ֖מָת בַּת־שׁ֣וּעַ אֵֽשֶׁת־יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּנָּ֣חֶם יְהוּדָ֗ה וַיַּ֜עַל עַל־גֹּֽזֲזֵ֤י צֹאנוֹ֙ ה֗וּא וְחִירָ֛ה רֵעֵ֥הוּ הָעֲדֻלָּמִ֖י תִּמְנָֽתָה׃

i18n.en: And in process of time the daughter of Shua, Yehudah's wife, died; and Yehudah was comforted, and went up unto his sheepshearers to Timnah, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite.

paragraphs.text: וַיֻּגַּ֥ד לְתָמָ֖ר לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּ֥ה חָמִ֛יךְ עֹלֶ֥ה תִמְנָ֖תָה לָגֹ֥ז צֹאנֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And it was told Tamar, saying, Behold, thy father-in-law goeth up to Timnah to shear his sheep.

paragraphs.text: וַתָּסַר֩ בִּגְדֵ֨י אַלְמְנוּתָ֜הּ מֵֽעָלֶ֗יהָ וַתְּכַ֤ס בַּצָּעִיף֙ וַתִּתְעַלָּ֔ף וַתֵּ֙שֶׁב֙ בְּפֶ֣תַח עֵינַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־דֶּ֣רֶךְ תִּמְנָ֑תָה כִּ֤י רָאֲתָה֙ כִּֽי־גָדַ֣ל שֵׁלָ֔ה וְהִ֕וא לֹֽא־נִתְּנָ֥ה ל֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃

i18n.en: And she put off from her the garments of her widowhood, and covered herself with her veil, and wrapped herself, and sat in the entrance of Einayim, which is by the way to Timnah; for she saw that Shelah was grown up, and she was not given unto him to wife.

paragraphs.commentary:
*be-fetach Einayim* is rendered **"in the entrance of Einayim"**, treating *Einayim* as a place-name (transliterated per the WoH proper-name convention; the same site as Enam, Josh 15:34). But *Einayim* is the dual of *ayin* ("eye" / "spring"), so *petach Einayim* can be heard as "the opening of (the) eyes" — a latent pun in a scene saturated with seeing and not-seeing: Yehudah will *see* her (v 15) yet *not recognise* his daughter-in-law because she had covered her face. Most translations read the toponym (ASV margin / NJPS "the entrance to Enaim"); commentators (Sarna, Alter) note the wordplay without dissolving the place-name.

The disguise-vocabulary: *tza'if* ("**veil**", the same wrap as Rivqah's, Gen 24:65) and *va-tit'allaf* (Hithpael of *alaf*, "and she **wrapped** herself / muffled herself"). Ironically, a covered face marked a respectable woman, not a prostitute — yet it is precisely the veil that makes Yehudah "take her for a *zonah*" (v 15). Surfaced at ASV-baseline; the pun and disguise-lexemes are pooled in the overlay (`petach-einayim-toponym-eyes-pun`). See Alter *Five Books of Moses* pp. 217-218.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּרְאֶ֣הָ יְהוּדָ֔ה וַֽיַּחְשְׁבֶ֖הָ לְזוֹנָ֑ה כִּ֥י כִסְּתָ֖ה פָּנֶֽיהָ׃

i18n.en: When Yehudah saw her, he took her for a prostitute; for she had covered her face.

paragraphs.commentary:
*va-yachsheveha le-zonah* ("he took her for a **prostitute**"). *zonah* is the narrator's word — the common prostitute (a Qal participle of z-n-h), the woman outside the legal-marriage framework. This is the **narrator's** classification; note that at vv 21-22 Hirah will switch to a different word, *qedeshah* (see commentary there). The lemma-decision *zonah* → "prostitute" is already settled in the central entry `zonah-prostitute-status-vocabulary-cross-corpus`, whose rationale explicitly names this verse; the entry's `appliesTo` has been extended to add GEN-WOH-38:15 (and GEN-WOH-38:24 for the v 24 finite z-n-h forms), closing the scope-gap the Translator flagged. No new lexical decision is invented here.

The seeing-pun continues: Yehudah's eyes are "open" (the *petach Einayim* of v 14) yet he sees only a veiled stranger, *ki kissetah paneha* ("because she had covered her face").

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֨ט אֵלֶ֜יהָ אֶל־הַדֶּ֗רֶךְ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הָֽבָה־נָּא֙ אָב֣וֹא אֵלַ֔יִךְ כִּ֚י לֹ֣א יָדַ֔ע כִּ֥י כַלָּת֖וֹ הִ֑וא וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ מַה־תִּתֶּן־לִּ֔י כִּ֥י תָב֖וֹא אֵלָֽי׃

i18n.en: And he turned unto her by the way, and said, Come, I pray thee, let me come in unto thee; for he knew not that she was his daughter-in-law. And she said, What wilt thou give me, that thou mayest come in unto me?

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אָנֹכִ֛י אֲשַׁלַּ֥ח גְּדִֽי־עִזִּ֖ים מִן־הַצֹּ֑אן וַתֹּ֕אמֶר אִם־תִּתֵּ֥ן עֵרָב֖וֹן עַ֥ד שָׁלְחֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: And he said, I will send thee a kid of the goats from the flock. And she said, Wilt thou give me a pledge, till thou send it?

paragraphs.commentary: *eravon* ("a **pledge**") is a genuine commercial-legal term — a security deposit held until payment (the root is loaned into Greek as *arrabon*, the "earnest / down-payment" of 2 Cor 1:22; Eph 1:14). The *gedi izzim* ("kid of the goats") Yehudah offers as the fee is itself a quiet measure-for-measure note, recalling the *se'ir izzim* (the goat whose blood marked Yosef's tunic, Gen 37:31): a goat enabled the deception of the father in ch 37; a goat now exposes the deceiver in ch 38. The pledge-triad is detailed at v 18 (`eravon-pledge-triad-signet-cord-staff`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מָ֣ה הָֽעֵרָבוֹן֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶתֶּן־לָּךְ֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר חֹתָֽמְךָ֙ וּפְתִילֶ֔ךָ וּמַטְּךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּיָדֶ֑ךָ וַיִּתֶּן־לָּ֛הּ וַיָּבֹ֥א אֵלֶ֖יהָ וַתַּ֥הַר לֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And he said, What pledge shall I give thee? And she said, Thy signet and thy cord, and thy staff that is in thy hand. And he gave them to her, and came in unto her, and she conceived by him.

paragraphs.commentary: The pledge-triad: *chotam* ("**signet** / seal"), *petil* ("**cord**" — the thread on which the seal was worn around the neck or wrist), and *matteh* ("**staff**"). Together they form an unmistakable personal-identity set — the ancient equivalent of one's signature, seal, and engraved walking-stick. The seal-and-cord are effectively one worn item (hence some render "seal and cord"). The same triad reappears verbatim at v 25 as the evidence that convicts Yehudah by his own *haker-na*. ASV-baseline "thy signet and thy cord, and thy staff" is kept; the *eravon* legal-pledge sense and the identity-token function are documented in the overlay (`eravon-pledge-triad-signet-cord-staff`). See Speiser *AB Genesis* p. 299; Sarna *JPS Genesis* pp. 268-269.

paragraphs.text: וַתָּ֣קָם וַתֵּ֔לֶךְ וַתָּ֥סַר צְעִיפָ֖הּ מֵעָלֶ֑יהָ וַתִּלְבַּ֖שׁ בִּגְדֵ֥י אַלְמְנוּתָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: And she arose, and went away, and put off her veil from her, and put on the garments of her widowhood.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח יְהוּדָ֜ה אֶת־גְּדִ֣י הָֽעִזִּ֗ים בְּיַד֙ רֵעֵ֣הוּ הָֽעֲדֻלָּמִ֔י לָקַ֥חַת הָעֵרָב֖וֹן מִיַּ֣ד הָאִשָּׁ֑ה וְלֹ֖א מְצָאָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: And Yehudah sent the kid of the goats by the hand of his friend the Adullamite, to receive the pledge from the woman's hand; but he found her not.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁאַ֞ל אֶת־אַנְשֵׁ֤י מְקֹמָהּ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אַיֵּ֧ה הַקְּדֵשָׁ֛ה הִ֥וא בָעֵינַ֖יִם עַל־הַדָּ֑רֶךְ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ לֹא־הָיְתָ֥ה בָזֶ֖ה קְדֵשָֽׁה׃

i18n.en: Then he asked the men of her place, saying, Where is the qedeshah, that was at Einayim by the way? And they said, There hath been no qedeshah here.

paragraphs.commentary:
The chapter's **major lexical crux**. The narrator twice called the disguised Tamar a *zonah* (a common prostitute, v 15), but Hirah, asking the locals after her, uses a *different* word: *ayyeh ha-qedeshah* ("where is the **qedeshah**?"). *qedeshah* is a feminine agent-noun from q-d-sh, "to be set apart / consecrated / holy" — literally a "consecrated / set-apart woman." The *zonah* → *qedeshah* shift raises the heavily contested question of cultic or "sacred" prostitution in the ancient Near East.

Two named mainstream positions, documented but not adjudicated: **(1) the traditional cultic reading** takes *qedeshah* / *qadesh* as cult-functionaries whose role included ritual sex ("cult / temple / sacred prostitute"), citing the pairing with cultic prohibitions in Deut 23:18-19 and Hos 4:14, the Deuteronomistic reform-notices (1-2 Kgs), and the Herodotus 1.199 / Lucian analogies (Albright; Speiser *AB Genesis* p. 300); **(2) the revisionist denial** holds that institutional "sacred prostitution" is a modern scholarly construct with no secure ancient basis — the sources are late, polemical, or misread, and *qedeshah* means simply a consecrated cult-servant, perhaps used here as a more polite upgrade of *zonah* (S. L. Budin, *The Myth of Sacred Prostitution in Antiquity*, 2008; J. G. Westenholz, HTR 82 [1989] 245-265; M. I. Gruber, UF 18 [1986] 133-148; P. A. Bird 1997).

The surface renders **"qedeshah" transliterated**, exactly so as not to prejudge the cultic question: "cult prostitute" would commit to position (1); "harlot" (ASV's collapse into *zonah*) would erase the deliberate lexical shift; "consecrated woman" would over-resolve toward position (2). Transliteration preserves the shift and flags the crux, consistent with the She'ol-type transliteration-of-the-irreducible-term precedent. Centrally housed by cross-corpus reach (Deut 23:18; Hos 4:14; 1-2 Kgs) in `qedeshah-consecrated-woman-sacred-prostitution-crux`.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֙שָׁב֙ אֶל־יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לֹ֣א מְצָאתִ֑יהָ וְגַ֨ם אַנְשֵׁ֤י הַמָּקוֹם֙ אָֽמְר֔וּ לֹא־הָיְתָ֥ה בָזֶ֖ה קְדֵשָֽׁה׃

i18n.en: And he returned to Yehudah, and said, I have not found her; and also the men of the place said, There hath been no qedeshah here.

paragraphs.commentary: *qedeshah* again, transliterated (see v 21). The townsmen's denial — *lo haytah va-zeh qedeshah* ("there has been no *qedeshah* here") — repeats Hirah's word, not the narrator's *zonah*, reinforcing the deliberate vocabulary-shift the transliteration preserves.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוּדָה֙ תִּֽקַּֽח־לָ֔הּ פֶּ֖ן נִהְיֶ֣ה לָב֑וּז הִנֵּ֤ה שָׁלַ֙חְתִּי֙ הַגְּדִ֣י הַזֶּ֔ה וְאַתָּ֖ה לֹ֥א מְצָאתָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: And Yehudah said, Let her take it to her, lest we be put to shame; behold, I sent this kid, and thou hast not found her.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֣י ׀ כְּמִשְׁלֹ֣שׁ חֳדָשִׁ֗ים וַיֻּגַּ֨ד לִֽיהוּדָ֤ה לֵֽאמֹר֙ זָֽנְתָה֙ תָּמָ֣ר כַּלָּתֶ֔ךָ וְגַ֛ם הִנֵּ֥ה הָרָ֖ה לִזְנוּנִ֑ים וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוּדָ֔ה הוֹצִיא֖וּהָ וְתִשָּׂרֵֽף׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass about three months after, that it was told Yehudah, saying, Tamar thy daughter-in-law hath played the harlot; and moreover, behold, she is with child by harlotry. And Yehudah said, Bring her forth, and let her be burnt.

paragraphs.commentary:
*zantah Tamar* ("Tamar hath **played the harlot**") and *harah li-znunim* ("she is with child by **harlotry**") are finite/abstract forms of the same z-n-h root as the participle *zonah* (v 15). The ASV-baseline register "played the harlot" / "by harlotry" is kept (rather than harmonizing to "prostituted herself"), preserving the distinction between the *verbal/abstract* forms here and the *substantive* participle ("prostitute") at v 15; the lemma-decision is governed by the central `zonah-prostitute-status-vocabulary-cross-corpus` entry, whose `appliesTo` now includes this verse. The irony is sharp: Yehudah, who himself solicited the roadside "prostitute," pronounces the death-sentence for the same offence.

*hotzi'uha ve-tissaref* ("Bring her forth, and let her be **burnt**") — the burning penalty (Niphal of *saraf*). Burning is the gravest execution-mode, reserved in the legal corpus for specific sexual offences (Lev 20:14; 21:9 — the priest's daughter who profanes herself by harlotry). Rendered ASV-baseline; uncontested, so no glossary entry is warranted.

paragraphs.text: הִ֣וא מוּצֵ֗את וְהִ֨יא שָׁלְחָ֤ה אֶל־חָמִ֙יהָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לְאִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁר־אֵ֣לֶּה לּ֔וֹ אָנֹכִ֖י הָרָ֑ה וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הַכֶּר־נָ֔א לְמִ֞י הַחֹתֶ֧מֶת וְהַפְּתִילִ֛ים וְהַמַּטֶּ֖ה הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

i18n.en: When she was brought forth, she sent to her father-in-law, saying, By the man, whose these are, am I with child: and she said, Discern, I pray thee, whose are these, the signet, and the cords, and the staff.

paragraphs.commentary:
*haker-na* ("**Discern, I pray thee**, whose are these") is the deliberate sibling to Gen 37:32, where the brothers send Yosef's blood-dipped tunic to Ya'aqov with the identical formula *haker-na* ("discern now whether it be thy son's coat"). The verb is the Hiphil of *nakar* ("recognise, identify, acknowledge"); Tamar turns the brothers' own deceiving-words back on Yehudah, now producing his own pledge-triad (the *chotemet*, *petilim*, *matteh* of v 18) as the evidence. This Gen 37 → 38 echo is one of the most-cited **measure-for-measure** literary links in Genesis: the goat (*se'ir izzim* / *gedi izzim*) and the *haker-na* that deceived the father in ch 37 now expose the deceiver in ch 38.

Per the ratified sibling-overlay pattern, this is recorded in a **separate** Gen 38 sibling entry (`haker-na-tamar-recognition-gen38`) that cross-references the Gen 37 entry (`haker-na-nakar-recognition-motif`) bidirectionally — NOT by extending the Gen 37 entry's `appliesTo`. ASV-baseline "Discern, I pray thee" matches the established Gen 37:32 surface so the verbal echo is reproducible in English. See Alter, *The Art of Biblical Narrative* ch. 1; Goldin, JBL 96 (1977) 27-44; Sarna *JPS Genesis* p. 270.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּכֵּ֣ר יְהוּדָ֗ה וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ צָֽדְקָ֣ה מִמֶּ֔נִּי כִּֽי־עַל־כֵּ֥ן לֹא־נְתַתִּ֖יהָ לְשֵׁלָ֣ה בְנִ֑י וְלֹֽא־יָסַ֥ף ע֖וֹד לְדַעְתָּֽה׃

i18n.en: And Yehudah acknowledged them, and said, She is more righteous than I; forasmuch as I gave her not to Shelah my son. And he knew her again no more.

paragraphs.commentary:
*va-yakker Yehudah* ("And Yehudah **acknowledged** them") closes the recognition-loop: the same Hiphil of *nakar* that Tamar invoked in v 25 (*haker-na*) — the deceiver of ch 37 now made the one who recognises (see `haker-na-tamar-recognition-gen38`).

*tzadqah mimmeni* ("**She is more righteous than I**") is a two-word crux turning on the preposition *min* in *mimmeni*. **(a)** Comparative (ASV/KJV): "more righteous *than* I." **(b)** Forensic / vindication (much modern scholarship): *tzadaq* is often legal — "to be in the right, to be vindicated" — so "she is **in the right**" (she had the just levirate claim Yehudah withheld), with *mimmeni* read comparatively ("more in the right than I") or causally ("she is in the right; the fault is *from* me"). NJPS, NRSV, and Alter lean forensic. The point is not abstract moral superiority but that, in the specific dispute over the withheld levir, Tamar had justice on her side — confirmed by Yehudah's own *ki al-ken lo netatiha le-Shelah beni* ("because I gave her not to Shelah my son").

ASV-baseline comparative "She is more righteous than I" is kept, with the forensic reading documented (`tzadqah-mimmeni-she-is-in-the-right`). The root tz-d-q is corpus-wide and already centrally anchored as a *noun* (Gen 15:6; 18:19), but this *verbal* forensic declaration is chapter-singular, so the crux is housed in the overlay. See HALOT s.v. *tzadaq*; B. Johnson in TDOT XII; Sarna *JPS Genesis* p. 270.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֖י בְּעֵ֣ת לִדְתָּ֑הּ וְהִנֵּ֥ה תְאוֹמִ֖ים בְּבִטְנָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass in the time of her travail, that, behold, twins were in her womb.

paragraphs.commentary: *te'omim* ("**twins**") — the same word used of the struggling twins Ya'aqov and Esav in the womb (Gen 25:24). The twin-birth that follows (the hand-first twin overtaken by the breach-bursting twin) reprises the Genesis younger-displaces-elder pattern. ASV-baseline; pooled into the birth-scene overlay entry (`zerach-shining-scarlet-etymology`).

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֥י בְלִדְתָּ֖הּ וַיִּתֶּן־יָ֑ד וַתִּקַּ֣ח הַמְיַלֶּ֗דֶת וַתִּקְשֹׁ֨ר עַל־יָד֤וֹ שָׁנִי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר זֶ֖ה יָצָ֥א רִאשֹׁנָֽה׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when she travailed, that one put out a hand: and the midwife took and bound upon his hand a scarlet thread, saying, This came out first.

paragraphs.commentary: *shani* ("**scarlet thread**") — the costly scarlet/crimson dye (cf. the tabernacle *tola'at shani*; Rachav's scarlet cord at Josh 2:18, itself an identification-marker, echoing here). The midwife binds it on the hand that emerged first, to mark the firstborn — but the order is then reversed when the other twin bursts through ahead (v 29). The scarlet mark becomes the implicit motivation for the name Zerach (v 30; see `zerach-shining-scarlet-etymology`). ASV-baseline "scarlet thread."

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֣י ׀ כְּמֵשִׁ֣יב יָד֗וֹ וְהִנֵּה֙ יָצָ֣א אָחִ֔יו וַתֹּ֕אמֶר מַה־פָּרַ֖צְתָּ עָלֶ֣יךָ פָּ֑רֶץ וַיִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ פָּֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, as he drew back his hand, that, behold, his brother came out: and she said, Wherefore hast thou made a breach for thyself? therefore his name was called Peretz.

paragraphs.commentary:
An explicit name-aetiology: *mah-paratzta alekha paretz* ("Wherefore hast thou made a **breach** for thyself?"), *va-yiqra shemo Paretz* ("and his name was called **Peretz**"). The name *Peretz* shares the root p-r-tz with the verb *paratz* ("break through, burst out, breach a wall") and the noun *peretz* ("a breach"; cf. *Ba'al-Peratzim*, 2 Sam 5:20, where YHWH "breaks through" like a *peretz mayim*). The naming plays on the firstborn-displacement: Zerach's hand emerged first, but Peretz "bursts through" ahead of him to be born first.

The name is **transliterated** ("Peretz") per the WoH convention, so the *paratzta / paretz / Peretz* wordplay survives the transliteration without glossing the name on the surface. Peretz heads the **Davidic-messianic line** (Ruth 4:18-22; 1 Chr 2:4-5; Matt 1:3) — decisive cross-corpus reach, hence central housing (`peretz-breach-davidic-ancestor-etymology`). See Sarna *JPS Genesis* p. 271; HALOT s.v. *prtz*.

paragraphs.text: וְאַחַר֙ יָצָ֣א אָחִ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־יָד֖וֹ הַשָּׁנִ֑י וַיִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ זָֽרַח׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And afterward came out his brother, that had the scarlet thread upon his hand: and his name was called Zerach.

paragraphs.commentary:
Unlike Peretz's explicit cognate aetiology (v 29), the name **Zerach** is given without a stated motivation — "his name was called Zerach," after the verse reidentifies him as "the one that had the *scarlet thread* upon his hand." Two etymologies are left in play: **(a)** the verb *zarach* ("to rise, shine, dawn" — of the sun; cf. *mizrach*, "the east / sunrise"), giving "shining / dawning / brightness"; and **(b)** the *shani* ("scarlet") thread of v 28, the red gleam on his hand reading as the visual motivation for the brightness-name. The two converge on "brightness."

The name is **transliterated** ("Zerach") per the WoH convention, with the etymology left unstated on the surface (as in the Hebrew) and both readings documented (`zerach-shining-scarlet-etymology`). See Sarna *JPS Genesis* p. 271; Alter *Five Books of Moses* pp. 219-220.
